studies.title: Rubber boot seal with frictional self-contact
studies.model_kind: 3-D assembly; half-domain symmetry
studies.geometry: Five decreasing-radius convolutions join a rubber boot to a rigid pipe. Original CAD view below; the source appendix gives the construction dimensions and operations. A 1 mm interference establishes the shrink fit.
studies.analysis: Nearly incompressible Yeoh rubber: c1 = 100 kPa, c2 = 6 kPa, c3 = -30 Pa. First mount the seal; then incrementally rotate the pipe 40 degrees about y, with the boot base fixed. Pipe/rubber friction = 0.7; rubber/rubber self-contact friction = 0.8. The source uses Nitsche contact.
studies.outputs: Deformed geometry, stress distribution and active contact surfaces through the rotation sequence (source Figures 2-4).
studies.reference: Published fields and deformation sequence; no numerical scalar grading reference or tolerance extracted. No new FEM run.
studies.notes: Difficulty assessment: complex thin geometry, finite strain, near incompressibility, interference and changing frictional self-contact.

studies.title: Layered piezoelectric valve and hyperelastic seal
studies.model_kind: 2-D axisymmetric analysis; 3-D assembly reference
studies.geometry: Annular bimorph actuator, alternating PZT/electrode layers, rubber seal and stainless-steel support. Figure 1 labels the components; Figure 2 resolves the actuator stack. Follow the source geometry sequence for dimensions.
studies.analysis: Couple electric potential and piezoelectric deformation to nonlinear seal contact. Alternate electrodes are grounded or driven; adjacent PZT layers have opposite polarization. The outer actuator rim is clamped. Voltage bends the actuator and presses the seal onto the annular opening.
studies.outputs: Seal strain, actuator stress, electric potential and contact-pressure distribution (source Figures 3-6).
studies.reference: The narrative reports maximum contact pressure 6e5 Pa. Its results text discusses 60 V while Figure 4 says 50 V; the operating point needs reconciliation before this value can be used for grading.
studies.notes: Difficulty assessment: thin multilayer geometry, coupled electromechanics and nonlinear contact. This source solves an axisymmetric model, not full 3-D fluid shutoff.

studies.title: Internally cooled turbine stator blade: thermal stress and creep
studies.model_kind: 3-D solid; sequential thermal/structural analysis
studies.geometry: Stator airfoil, mounting platforms and an internal cooling duct. The base study imports turbine_stator.mphbin; these CAD views are not a complete dimensioned drawing. Reference CAD is needed for exact reconstruction.
studies.analysis: Start with the linked base study: GTD111 DS alloy, temperature-dependent properties, gas at 1150 K, coolant at 650 K and roller/spring supports. Then hold the solved temperature field constant for 400 h and evolve isotropic secondary Norton creep: A = 2.5e-23 /h, n = 6.75, reference stress 1 MPa, activation energy 350 kJ/mol, activation reference temperature 900 K.
studies.outputs: Temperature, displacement, stress relaxation and creep-strain fields over operating time, as displayed by the source studies.
studies.reference: Published solution fields; no numerical scalar grading reference or tolerance extracted. The tutorial assumes isotropic creep despite the directionally solidified alloy.
studies.notes: Difficulty assessment: complex internal CAD, temperature-dependent properties and nonlinear time evolution.

studies.title: Compound gear train: tooth contact and housing vibration
studies.model_kind: 2-D contact FEM + 3-D multibody/elastic housing
studies.geometry: Two spur-gear pairs, three shafts and an elastic housing. Each pinion/wheel has 20/30 teeth, 50/75 mm pitch diameter, 25-degree pressure angle and 10 mm width. Source geometry parameters and imported housing define the assembly.
studies.analysis: First compute gear-mesh stiffness by rotating a contacting 2-D steel gear pair through mesh cycles with 0.5-degree twist. Use that varying stiffness in the transient assembly: input speed 600 rad/s, output torque 100 N m. Shafts/gears are rigid in this second stage; the housing is elastic.
studies.outputs: Mesh stiffness versus angle; tooth stresses; gear contact forces; shaft motion; housing acceleration and frequency content.
studies.reference: The source reports dominant housing frequencies near 550 and 2000 Hz. These are approximate spectral observations, not mesh-converged scalar grading references.
studies.notes: Difficulty assessment: involute geometry, changing tooth contact and sequential contact/dynamics analysis; not full flexible-body 3-D tooth contact.
